layout: shared daily grid: series[k].v[i] is the value on t[i] (UTC day start); null = no measurement that day

series.name: Heliospheric protons 3-4.6 MeV
series.dataset: SPDF voyager2/crs/additional_data/one_day (not in CDAWeb as a daily set) (H bin 1)
series.description: CRS lowest-energy hydrogen bin: anomalous cosmic rays and termination-shock particles, which are made inside the heliosphere. Rises toward and across the termination shock; collapses at the heliopause, where the remaining level is the galactic cosmic-ray contribution in this bin.

series.name: Low-energy ions 0.54-0.99 MeV
series.description: LECP Z>=1 ions (mostly protons), 1-day scan-averaged differential intensity, channel PL06. The team's daily file carries no background correction note; at both heliopause crossings this channel falls only ~4x, to a floor that is most likely instrument background from penetrating cosmic rays rather than interstellar ions, so crs_low shows the heliopause drop more cleanly.

series.name: Galactic cosmic-ray protons 130.3-344.0 MeV
series.dataset: SPDF voyager2/crs/additional_data/one_day (not in CDAWeb as a daily set)
series.description: Galactic cosmic-ray protons: CRS daily hydrogen differential fluxes summed as sum(j*dE) over the 130.3-344.0 MeV bins (gaps between bins are not filled). An integral intensity, not the CRS team's >70 MeV count rate.

series.name: Proton density
series.description: Voyager 2 Plasma Science (PLS) daily average; density is the fit value (column 12), speed = |(VR,VT,VN)|.

series.name: Bulk flow speed
series.description: Voyager 2 Plasma Science (PLS) daily average; density is the fit value (column 12), speed = |(VR,VT,VN)|.

notes: Stone et al. 2008, Nature 454, 71; Richardson et al. 2008, Nature 454, 63. Voyager 2 crossed the moving shock several times around 2007-08-30/09-01; the plasma instrument saw the solar wind slow down (pls_speed).
